subject: Unexpected interaction of xlim and scale... name=

messages.author: 519455d3bf64680d
messages.subject: Unexpected interaction of xlim and scale... name=
parts:
When xlim() or ylim() is specified, name labels (at least as specified
to scale_continuous) are suppressed.

Consider:
library(data)

ggplot(data=diamonds)+geom_smooth(aes(x=carat, y=price))+
scale_x_continuous(name="X axis") + scale_y_continuous(name="Yaxis")

#(Labels are substituted on axes, as expected)

ggplot(data=diamonds)+geom_smooth(aes(x=carat, y=price))+
scale_x_continuous(name="X axis") + scale_y_continuous(name="Yaxis")+
xlim(1,4)+ylim(300, 16000)
# (Variable names appear on axes, despite specification to scale_continuous


#(Variable names appear on axes)

Is this a feature?

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Unexpected interaction of xlim and scale... name=
parts:
The order matters...

ggplot(data=diamonds)+geom_smooth(aes(x=carat, y=price))+
    xlim(1,4)+ylim(300, 16000)+scale_x_continuous(name="X axis") + scale_y_continuous(name="Yaxis")

Put the names last and they stick. Put the names in the middle and the limit changes overwrite the variable names you supply. Not sure this is the way it should work, but this is the way that it does. 

Brandon

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Unexpected interaction of xlim and scale... name=
parts:
Hi

Note that if you call scale_x_*() after xlim(), then the xlim() is ignored.
xlim() is just like a syntax suger, and both xlim() and scale_x_*()
return scale object.
So if you want to set both limits and names, set them in the call of scale_x_*()

ggplot(data=diamonds)+geom_smooth(aes(x=carat,
y=price))+scale_x_continuous(name="X axis", xlim=c(1,4))

--

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Unexpected interaction of xlim and scale... name=
parts:
Hi:

Another thing: if you want *exactly* the x and y limits specified, you
should use coord_cartesian(). Compare the following two
specifications:

ggplot(data=diamonds)+geom_smooth(aes(x=carat, y=price))+
scale_x_continuous(name = 'X axis', xlim = c(1, 4)) +
scale_y_continuous(name = 'Y axis', xlim = c(300, 16000))

ggplot(data=diamonds)+geom_smooth(aes(x=carat, y=price))+
coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1, 4), ylim = c(300, 16000)) +
labs(x = 'X axis', y = 'Y axis')

In the latter case, flipping the order of coord_cartesian() and labs()
makes no difference.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.author: 519455d3bf64680d
messages.subject: Re: Unexpected interaction of xlim and scale... name=
parts:
Thanks for the input. Clearly order matters.

Expressed differently, the issue is that xlim and ylim can be called
either as independent functions, or as functions/arguments nested within
scale_ and coord_ function. Only when xlim or ylim are used
independently does this problem arise. Perhaps the standard coding
practice should be to use these functions within calls to scale or coord..

Many thanks,

Rob
